content: Misfortune may conceal a blessing, just as fortune may harbor sorrow.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Sai weng shi ma (塞翁失马) — Huainanzi (Classical Taoist Parable)
explanation: When the old man of the frontier lost his horse, neighbors pitied him, but he asked, 'How do you know this is bad?' The horse returned leading a herd of wild stallions. Life's events are never isolated chapters; every catastrophe carries the seed of grace, and every triumph requires vigilance.
practicalInsight: When a seemingly terrible event derails your plans today, suspend judgment. Meet it with calm equanimity and watch how the story unfolds.
reflectionPrompt: What past disappointment or rejection ultimately redirected your footsteps toward a far greater blessing?
